Katanga Mining Ltd Names New Chief Operating Officer to Oversee Congo Operations

Katanga Mining Ltd announced on Tuesday the appointment of Jean-Paul Mukendi as its new Chief Operating Officer, as the company seeks to strengthen its operational leadership in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Mukendi, a mining executive with over 20 years of experience in Africa’s metals sector, will assume responsibility for overseeing Katanga’s production and expansion activities at its flagship copper and cobalt mines in Lualaba province. The appointment is effective immediately, the company said in a statement.

“We are delighted to welcome Jean-Paul Mukendi to the executive team,” said Katanga Mining Ltd’s Chief Executive Officer, Alice van der Merwe. “His deep industry knowledge and proven track record in operational excellence will be invaluable as we continue to optimize production and enhance safety standards across our Congolese operations.”

Mukendi joins Katanga Mining Ltd from Lubumbashi-based Equator Resources, where he most recently served as Chief Operations Manager. He holds degrees in mining engineering from the University of Lubumbashi and an MBA from the African School of Economics.

In a call with reporters, Mukendi said his immediate priorities would include boosting output at the Tshipuka and Kamoto mining complexes, investing in workforce training, and working closely with local communities. “The DRC is central to the global energy transition, and Katanga Mining has a unique role to play in responsibly supplying copper and cobalt to world markets,” Mukendi said. “I look forward to collaborating with our skilled teams and partners to deliver on our ambitious growth targets.”

Analysts welcomed the move, citing Mukendi’s familiarity with the regulatory and logistical landscape in the DRC. “Katanga’s operations are among the largest in the region, and local expertise is vital to navigating infrastructure and permitting challenges,” said Pascal Ilunga, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Mining Insight.

According to industry data, Katanga Mining Ltd produced 180,000 tonnes of copper and 17,000 tonnes of cobalt in 2023, making it one of the country’s leading exporters of battery metals. The company has committed to increasing output by 10% this year, in line with rising demand from manufacturers worldwide.

The Chamber of Mines of the DRC also welcomed the appointment. “We congratulate Mr. Mukendi and look forward to working together to ensure sustainable development in the sector,” said Chamber spokesperson Isabelle Kalume.

Katanga Mining Ltd employs more than 3,500 people in the DRC and operates several community development initiatives in the Lualaba and Haut-Katanga provinces.
